subject: community-medicine
title: Congenital Rubella Syndrome: Timing, Triad and Prevention

steps.title: A mild rash with a nine month shadow
steps.tx: **Rubella** in children and adults is a brief, mild illness of low fever, pink rash and tender lymph nodes behind the ears and in the neck, often passing unnoticed entirely. Its public health importance is entirely fetal: infection in early pregnancy can devastate organ development, so surveillance counts pregnant exposures, not playground rashes.
steps.say: A trivial rash in children, a catastrophe in early pregnancy. Rubella programmes exist for the fetus, not the febrile child in front of you.

vis.alt: Clinical features of rubella including rash and lymphadenopathy
vis.caption: Rubella: fine pink rash with posterior auricular lymphadenopathy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.title: Risk by week of gestation
steps.tx: **Gestational timing** decides damage: infection in the first ten to twelve weeks infects most fetuses and causes defects in the great majority, with risk falling steeply after sixteen weeks and deafness the latest possible injury into the second trimester. The same maternal rash is therefore an emergency at eight weeks and a lesser threat at twenty.
steps.say: First twelve weeks carry the worst risk, fading after sixteen, deafness last to leave. Week of pregnancy converts a mild rash into a prognosis.

steps.title: The classic triad
steps.tx: The **classic triad** of congenital rubella syndrome is sensorineural deafness, eye defects led by cataract, and congenital heart disease led by patent ductus arteriosus and pulmonary artery stenosis. Deafness is the commonest single defect and may be the only one, presenting late when newborn hearing screening or speech delay finally betrays it.
steps.say: Deafness, cataracts, patent ductus. Hearing loss leads and often hides alone until speech delays. Every unexplained congenital deafness deserves a rubella history.

steps.title: Beyond the triad: the expanded syndrome
steps.tx: **Expanded features** include purpuric blueberry muffin skin lesions from extramedullary blood formation, enlarged liver and spleen, low platelets, bone lucencies, meningoencephalitis, microcephaly and developmental disability. Infected infants shed virus from throat and urine for many months, infecting susceptible pregnant contacts in nurseries and clinics.
steps.say: Blueberry muffin purpura, big liver and spleen, low platelets, small head. These infants shed virus for months. Nursery contacts who are pregnant need protection.

steps.title: Confirming infection in mother and baby
steps.tx: **Laboratory confirmation** in the infant rests on rubella IgM at birth, persistent or rising IgG beyond the expected maternal antibody decay, and virus detection in throat or urine samples. Maternal diagnosis uses IgM and IgG avidity where available. Documentation matters for counselling, cohorting and the child's long term follow up plan.
steps.say: Infant IgM, IgG that refuses to decay, virus in throat or urine. Maternal avidity dates the infection. Confirm properly; labels follow this child for life.

steps.title: Salt and pepper retinopathy
steps.tx: **Pigmentary retinopathy** gives the fundus a salt and pepper mottling that is the commonest eye finding yet usually spares vision, unlike dense congenital cataracts, microphthalmos and infantile glaucoma which threaten sight directly. A white pupil reflex in a newborn with maternal rash history is rubella until ophthalmology proves otherwise.
steps.say: Salt and pepper fundus mottling usually spares vision; cataract and glaucoma do not. White pupil plus rash history means urgent eye referral.

steps.title: Prevention is vaccination before pregnancy
steps.tx: **Rubella containing vaccine** given in childhood measles rubella campaigns and to susceptible adolescent girls and women before pregnancy is the only prevention, because no treatment alters fetal infection once acquired. Live vaccine is avoided during pregnancy itself and pregnancy is deferred briefly after vaccination, a counselling point every antenatal clinic repeats.
steps.say: Vaccinate before pregnancy; nothing treats fetal infection afterwards. Live vaccine avoids pregnancy itself, with a short deferral after the dose. Timing is everything.

steps.title: Caring for the infected infant
steps.tx: **Infection control** cohorts congenitally infected infants away from non immune pregnant staff and visitors, with contact precautions for secretions and urine through the first year unless repeat testing shows shedding has stopped. Families need explicit warning that grandparents and pregnant relatives are the people this cheerful baby can silently harm.
steps.say: Cohort the baby, precautions with urine and secretions, shield pregnant contacts for months. Families rarely guess their infant endangers a pregnant grandmother.

steps.title: Elimination goals and surveillance
steps.tx: **Rubella elimination** rides on measles platforms: combined vaccine, coverage above ninety five percent, surveillance of congenital rubella syndrome through sentinel sites auditing deafness, cataract and heart defects in infants, plus rash fever surveillance with laboratory confirmation. Each detected syndrome case marks a chain of missed vaccination years earlier.
steps.say: One syndrome baby audits years of missed doses. Sentinel surveillance of deafness, cataract and heart defects keeps programmes honest about that debt.
